title_native: ドラゴンボール超 ビルス
episode_title: A God's Appetite and Vegeta's Worst Nightmare
pullquote: The real punchline isn't Vegeta getting dragged through a family resort; it's the sheer terror rattling behind his clenched teeth the second he realizes Beerus is on the move. That instant flip from goofy family comedy into universe-shattering dread is Toriyama storytelling at its finest.
quick_take: The real punchline isn't Vegeta getting dragged through a family resort; it's the sheer terror rattling behind his clenched teeth the second he realizes Beerus is on the move. That instant flip from goofy family comedy into universe-shattering dread is Toriyama storytelling at its finest.
one_sentence_verdict: A razor-sharp mix of hilarious slice-of-life discomfort and cosmic dread that sets up the terrifying scale of the God of Destruction.
synopsis_paragraphs: You can feel the tension snap like a dry twig the second this episode shifts gears. One minute you are watching pure, unfiltered Dragon Ball comedy with Vegeta looking completely miserable surrounded by luxury resort crowds, and the next, a cold silence drops right over the galaxy. That sudden chill when North Kaio starts trembling isn't played for cheap laughs. It is genuine existential dread, reminding you that the brief peace everyone fought so hard for after Majin Buu is hanging by a thread.

What makes this enhanced cut breathe so well is the pacing of that contrast. Instead of rushing headlong into punch-ups, the production lets the domestic awkwardness sit there just long enough to make Beerus feel truly terrifying by comparison. Beerus isn't some boastful tyrant with a grand villain speech; he is an ancient, capricious force of nature who might blow up half a sector just because his snack was slightly too greasy. You feel the walls closing in on the cast, even under the blinding midday sun.
sakuga_paragraphs:
* **Craft point:** Watch how Director of Photography Yousuke Motoki handles the shift between Earth and deep space. The resort scenes are drenched in warm, saturated sunlight, but whenever the cut snaps to Beerus floating near his temple, the palette hardens into cold purples and stark edge-lighting that makes the God of Destruction look genuinely out of this world.
* **Craft point:** Chief Animation Director Tadayoshi Yamamuro keeps Vegeta's character acting anchored on brutal micro-timing. Look at the beat right before Vegeta reacts to Kaio's mental warning: the animation freezes the Prince's posture completely rigid for a couple of frames before a sudden, tiny eye twitch breaks the pose, visually timing out the exact split-second his pride melts into panic.
story_paragraphs:
* **「ベジータの胃が痛い回」 (Vegeta's stomach ulcer episode):** As soon as the credits rolled, late-night X and 5ch threads exploded with this exact phrase. Japanese fandom loves using 'stomach ache' slang whenever a prideful warrior is trapped in an impossible, high-stress social grind, and watching Vegeta squirm while trying to keep the peace had everyone cheering.
* **「山ちゃんの破壊神ボイス、やっぱり別格」 (Yama-chan's God of Destruction voice really is on another level):** Timelines consistently praised Kouichi Yamadera (widely adored by his domestic nickname 'Yama-chan'). Fans were glued to the sheer range in his vocal tone, raving about how naturally he slides from a lazy cat complaining about food into a terrifying deity capable of wiping out star systems with a tap of his nail.
voice_paragraphs: * **Craft point:** Kouichi Yamadera delivers a masterclass in quiet menace as Beerus, purring with sleepy elegance before snapping into icy boredom that sends shivers down your spine. Opposite that restraint, Ryo Horikawa turns Vegeta inside out, letting a frantic, suppressed choke break into his iconic gravelly sneer as the Saiyan Prince realizes he cannot muscle his way out of this meeting.
takeaway_paragraphs: A razor-sharp mix of hilarious slice-of-life discomfort and cosmic dread that sets up the terrifying scale of the God of Destruction. Stream the full remastered episode right now on Netflix and Crunchyroll.
